extracted.intended_audience: users of Mathematics Stack Exchange asking homework questions (students/posters seeking help)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to post homework-style mathematics questions on Mathematics Stack Exchange so they are appropriate, answerable, and likely to receive helpful responses. Covers what to include, how to phrase the question, and expectations about answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of homework questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The site does not discourage any specific category of questions, as long as it is mathematical. However, search through previously asked questions because homework questions are often duplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate questions — especially homework-type ones — will be closed. Do initial research / searching before posting to avoid asking an already-answered question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect your institution's honor code
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether your school or instructor allows you to consult others or post exact homework questions online is determined by your institution's honor code or class policies; you should check with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your teacher whether asking a homework question here is appropriate before posting; compliance with classroom rules is your responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put effort into formulating your question
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not just copy and paste the exact question text from your homework sheet; make an effort to formulate your question as a genuine question rather than an imperative assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imperative phrasing like 'Show that...', 'Compute...', 'Prove or find a counterexample: ...' is discouraged as it reads like giving an assignment and turns people off. Rephrase in your own words and explain what you need help with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote and reference sources when copying
rubrics_metrics.description: If copying the problem statement is necessary, explicitly quote the text and give a reference to the source (e.g., textbook title, author, edition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting and giving a source helps others refer to context and is good practice when you must reproduce the original problem verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide the context (course, textbook, level)
rubrics_metrics.description: State what kind of course it is and what textbook (or other source) you use so answers can be tailored to your level and use appropriate methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect answerers to assume your background; indicating context prevents receiving solutions that rely on advanced machinery you haven't seen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all relevant definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When asking about material beyond basic college calculus, include the definitions you are using, since many mathematical objects have several equivalent definitions that affect what must be proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the framework and definitions because a statement trivial under one definition may be nontrivial under another; this helps answerers target the correct approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show your work / partial attempts
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any partial work or attempts you have made so answerers can gauge where you are stuck and whether you are asking for help or for someone to do the homework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing work bolsters your claim that you are not just seeking free solutions, helps tailor the length/detail of answers (short hint vs full explanation), and prevents answerers from covering ground you already understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer all relevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all information relevant to the question upfront; it's a waste of everyone's time if answerers must ask for missing details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include necessary assumptions, domain restrictions, prior lemmas, notation conventions, or any details a reader would need to produce a correct answer without follow-up requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not expect complete solutions; focus on learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The community generally avoids giving complete, copy-able solutions that do not help a student learn, because that encourages using the site as a free homework service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers may be hint-based or partial to encourage learning; you may later edit the question or post your own full solution once you've learned. See related discussion about pedagogical answering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid posting long scans/images of printed documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Including pages and pages of printed documents as images is discouraged; it's better to state the problem and relevant parts in your own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large image attachments make questions harder to use; prefer typed text, quote only the necessary parts, and summarize context instead of dumping many pages of images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be polite in phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase your request as a question rather than an assignment; imperative tones are impolite and unhelpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asking 'How can I show that...' or 'Why does X imply Y?' is preferable to simply 'Prove that...'; polite phrasing is more likely to engage answerers constructively.
